title: Maryland Find-a-Program
summary: A statewide search platform helping families find high-quality child care.
description:
Designed and built as a modern replacement for a legacy directory, Find a Program is a
        public-facing search tool that helps parents and guardians across Maryland locate
        high-quality child care programs. Built from scratch as a Vue and TypeScript single-page
        application, the platform utilizes an existing API and uses centralized client-side state
        management to deliver fast, responsive search results across all devices. I led the product
        design and front-end development, including early prototyping and stakeholder presentations
        to the Maryland Department of Education. The design goal was to make searching for child
        care feel as intuitive as booking a hotel- centered around a single, flexible search input
        that understands location and intent, with optional filters available for refining
        results. This approach replaced a slow, checkbox-heavy legacy experience with a streamlined,
        mobile-first interface that prioritizes clarity, performance, and ease of use. The final
        system serves thousands of families statewide and supports discovery of programs with
        quality ratings and eligibility for Child Care Scholarships.

title: Campbells - Pace Salsa
summary: An interactive brand experience blending playful creativity with custom engineering.
description:
PacePort was a promotional mini-site created for Pace Salsa that allowed users to upload a photo and place their face into a customizable, "south-of-the-border" themed scene. Designed as a playful "face-in-hole" experience, the application let users decorate their scene with clothing, props, and accessories before exporting a final image they could download or share on social media.

I designed and built the application from scratch with minimal creative direction beyond provided brand assets. The project combined extensive Flash/ActionScript development with JavaScript and a custom PHP/MySQL backend, which I architected and delivered for Campbell's to host internally. The system handled image uploads, compositing, and final jpeg generation, balancing performance, reliability, and user-friendly interaction in a technically demanding environment.

Completed under a tight three-week timeline, the project required rapid problem-solving and independent research, pulling together disparate techniques and sample code into a cohesive, production-ready application. The result was a polished, highly interactive marketing experience that aligned with Pace's brand voice while demonstrating the ability to deliver complex, custom software under real-world constraints.

title: Porter Cable Tools
summary: An interactive product tour showcasing tools through motion and video.
description:
Developed as a highly interactive virtual product tour for Porter-Cable tools, this project combined 360-degree product visualization, video, and animated feature callouts into a cohesive, brand-forward experience. Designed to feel tactile and engaging, the tour allowed users to explore tools from multiple angles while highlighting key features through motion graphics and guided interaction.

I designed and built the application from scratch, working closely with Porter-Cable's ad agency to align with established branding while independently capturing and producing the 360-degree product photography. The system was implemented using extensive Flash/ActionScript development with JavaScript and a structured XML-based data layer that made it easy to configure and reuse the tour framework across multiple tools. That architecture enabled the creation of roughly ten distinct product tours with minimal duplication, each driven by easily-editable backend data.

The final result was a polished, animation-rich product experience that balanced visual impact with technical flexibility-- demonstrating an ability to translate static product assets into interactive, reusable software systems under real-world production constraints.

title: Versant Strategies
summary: Public-facing marketing and content site for a public affairs firm.
description: This legacy site was recently re-architected as a Vue single-page application to support clearer content presentation, improved mobile performance, and long-term maintainability. The rebuild introduced centralized client-side state management for dynamic content and emphasized responsive layout architecture with mobile-first CSS. A lightweight backend integration supports routine content updates while keeping the front-end fast and focused.

title: Rich Valley Gymnastics
summary: A mobile-first site for a local gymnastics program.
description: Originally built as a PHP multi-page website, Rich Valley Gymnastics eventually outgrew its original structure, especially when it came to  modern expectations for mobile-responsiveness. It was recently rebuilt as a modern Vue/TypeScript single-page application, with PHP retained only for lightweight API calls. The renovation focused on making the experience genuinely usable for parents on phones and tablets, pairing a database-driven scheduling system with a responsive layout that works comfortably across all screen sizes.

title: Sani-Hands Wipes
summary: An interactive mini-site promoting hand hygiene.
description:
Developed as an interactive, kid-friendly game to promote proper hand sanitizing, this project translated Sani-Hands' health messaging into a playful, arcade-style experience inspired by the classic Frogger. Players guided characters through a grimy, germ-filled environment-- dodging obstacles and hazards-- to safely reach the other side, reinforcing the importance of hygiene through action rather than instruction.

Working in collaboration with Sani-Hands' advertising agency, I designed and built the game using Flash/ActionScript and JavaScript, integrating provided brand assets while creating additional custom artwork for characters, germs, and environmental obstacles. The project balanced educational intent with approachable gameplay, ensuring the experience remained engaging for children while clearly aligning with the Sani-Hands Kids product line. The completed application was delivered to Sani-Hands for hosting and distribution as part of a broader national marketing and education effort.

title: Delta Machinery
summary: A reusable interactive product tour platform for precision woodworking tools.
description:
Developed as a highly interactive virtual product tour for Delta Machinery, this project showcased woodworking tools through 360-degree rotation, video, animated feature highlights, and guided navigation. Designed to emphasize precision, reliability, and craftsmanship, the experience allowed users to explore complex tools in a clear, tactile way before ever seeing them in person.

The application was built using a reusable interactive framework originally developed for similar national brands, combining extensive Flash/ActionScript development with JavaScript and a structured XML-driven data layer. That architecture made it possible to configure multiple product tours efficiently while preserving a consistent interaction model and brand-specific presentation. Delta-provided photography and assets were integrated into a fully custom interface designed to align with existing brand standards and visual language.

By separating content from behavior, the system supported rapid production of multiple tours with shared functionality-- demonstrating an early focus on modular design, maintainability, and scalable interactive systems. The result was a polished, on-brand product experience used to support national marketing and retail efforts.

title: PA Forestry Association
summary: A mobile-friendly rebuild of a legacy site supporting forest stewardship and education.
description:
This project focused on rebuilding the Pennsylvania Forestry Association's legacy website from the ground up to improve usability, accessibility, and mobile support while preserving the organization's established visual identity. The existing design and content direction were retained, with selective refinements made as needed to support a modern, responsive layout and improved performance across devices.

The work involved extensive HTML and CSS restructuring to translate a desktop-oriented site into a mobile-friendly experience suitable for phones and tablets. Emphasis was placed responsive layout techniques and maintainable styles that allowed the organization's educational content and advocacy work to remain clear and readable in the field as well as at the desk. The result was a technically modernized site that respected the original design intent while bringing the platform forward to meet contemporary usage expectations.

title: Maryland Accreditation
summary: A statewide accreditation platform supporting quality early childhood education.
description:
Designed and built from scratch as a modern replacement for a legacy system, Maryland Accreditation is a state-level web platform that supports licensed child care centers and public pre-K programs as they pursue accreditation. Built as a Vue and TypeScript single-page application with centralized client-side state management, the system guides programs through a multi-stage accreditation process: standards review, self-appraisal, improvement planning, validation, and ongoing support, all while remaining fully usable on mobile devices. I led product design and front-end architecture, developing and pitching the initial prototype to the Maryland Department of Education and aligning a cross-functional development team around a shared UX vision. The interface was intentionally designed to feel familiar and trustworthy, prioritizing clear workflows, accessible design, and human-centered language. Dashboards, messaging, and visual hierarchy were carefully shaped to help users understand where they are in the process, what they've completed, and what comes next-- reducing confusion in a system with inherently complex requirements.

Beyond improving the experience for participating programs, the rebuilt platform significantly streamlined internal workflows for Maryland EXCELS administrators. Manual processes and ad hoc workarounds were replaced with in-system automation wherever possible, reducing administrative overhead while improving consistency, visibility, and support across the accreditation lifecycle.
